Her discovery led to effective treatments and combination therapies for malaria.

card.title: Discovery of Morphine
card.body: Morphine was first extracted as an active alkaloid from the opium poppy plant in December 1804 by German pharmacist Friedrich Sertürner in Paderborn. He noticed its sedative effects and reported his findings in 1805. Sertürner named the substance morphium, after Morpheus, the Greek god of dreams, due to its sleep-inducing properties. Morphine was initially marketed as a pain medication and treatment for addiction in 1817.

card.title: Vanilla's sweet journey
card.body: Vanillin, the star of sweet treats, flavors ice cream and chocolate, making up 75% of its use in the flavor industry. It also adds a creamy note to drinks like cream soda and hides less pleasant tastes in medicines and cleaning products.
